newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ahold eyes further U.S. acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Ahold eyes further U.S. acquisitions.

text.p: Dutch supermarkets group Ahold NV remains on the lookout for further acquisitions on the U.S. east coast, chairman Cees van der Hoeven told reporters before the company's annual meeting on Tuesday.
"We are looking at sales of one billion dollars plus... It's quality operators that we're looking for," he said.

Van der Hoeven and board member Rob Zwartendijk said Ahold had already achieved critical mass in the U.S. where it has annual sales of $11.2 billion, but could further exploit its economies of scale by making additional acquisitions there.
Until now Ahold has focused on east coast locations, but Zwartendijk, chief executive of Ahold USA, said the company was also interested in opportunities a little further west.
"We are going a bit more inland, maybe out to Chicago, but not much more west than that," he said.
Expansion within or close to the region where Ahold already operates made most sense because it would bring the most synergy benefits, he said.
"In the area that we are talking about, there are still a lot of interesting companies," Zwartendijk said.
Zwartendijk said Ahold was currently holding friendly talks with various companies in the region.

Zwartendijk predicted a wave of mergers and acquisitions in the U.S. supermarkets business, noting that in Europe the five biggest retailers had some 80 percent of the market, while in the U.S. the top five had about 20 percent of the market.
"There's a lot more consolidation to come and we will play a part in it," Zwartendijk said.
Van der Hoeven repeated an earlier statement that Ahold would issue shares in order to finance major acquisitions.

"Anything costing more than 500 million guilders...will be, at least partially financed through the issue of shares, but only if it immediately contributes to growth in earnings per share," Van der Hoeven said.
